subject: BYOK transition playlist and subprocessor timeline
messages:
From: Robert Chen <robert.chen@novamed.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>, legal@novamed.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: BYOK transition plan & subprocessors

Sean / Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare procurement paperwork for our Private Deployment (VPC + on-prem fallback), legal asked us to provide a concise transition plan showing: the BYOK handoff steps, where operator access is required, and a timeline for notifying/contracting subprocessors. Can you share a playlist-style runbook plus any evidence pack that NovaMed can attach to our DPA?

Two quick asks from our side:
- We need the list of subprocessors that will handle telemetry/ops for the private deployment and the expected notification window for each (30/60/90 days).
- We need confirmation of whether Redwood will accept a NovaMed-managed CMK in our cloud envelope or if an on-prem HSM pattern is required for certain modules.

I attached a short procurement checklist that our Sourcing team will use. If you can send an initial playlist and a proposed timeline by end of week, that helps us keep the procurement window open.

Attachments: Procurement_Checklist_NovaMed.xlsx (referenced)

Best,
Robert
Robert Chen
Head of IT Sourcing, NovaMed
robert.chen@novamed.com

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK transition plan & subprocessors

Robert —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a compact "BYOK transition playlist" (BYOK_Playlist_v1.xlsx) and a draft subprocessor notification timeline (Subproc_Timeline_v2.pdf). High level summary below so your legal and sourcing teams can see the key commitments at a glance:

- BYOK patterns supported: 
  1) Cloud CMK (NovaMed-managed key in your cloud KMS) — supported for hosted control plane + VPC deployment. Redwood will perform key-wrapping and will not persist plaintext keys.
 2) On-prem HSM gateway — supported for fully air-gapped modules; requires on-prem gateway and short-term key escrow protocol for emergency recovery.

- Operator access windows: standard maintenance windows are scheduled and require approval via the mutual action plan (MAP). For private deployments we propose:
  - Routine ops: 0-2 hour ephemeral access (audit logged)
  - Break-glass: limited to on-call SREs with documented justification and notarized request; full telemetry snapshot only with customer's signed consent.

- Subprocessor timeline (in attached PDF):
  - Tier 1 (core runtime telemetry & scheduling): 60-day notice, contract addendum required.
  - Tier 2 (support tooling, telemetry analytics): 90-day notice.
  - Emergency short-term partners (cloud infra providers): typically covered by platform SLA; we list named providers and their roles in the PDF.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal: confirm the notification windows are acceptable or provide counter windows.
2) Security: agree on the break-glass attestation language in the DPA annex.
3) Procurement: we will prepare a DocuSign packet for the MAP and subproc addendum once timelines are locked.

Notes: the playlist includes checklist rows you can paste into your procurement artifact (key custody acceptance, HSM gateway readiness, operator rosters).

Attachments: BYOK_Playlist_v1.xlsx, Subproc_Timeline_v2.pdf

I'll be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow if you want to walk through the playlist with Irene and Karthik.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Field Security, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK transition plan & subprocessors

Robert / Sean —

Thanks — I reviewed the playlist and timeline and wanted to clarify two technical points your security team typically asks about:

1) Key provisioning and rotation model: our recommended pattern for NovaMed is "envelope + ephemeral session key" where the NovaMed CMK wraps the session key; Redwood never stores the unwrapped session key longer than the token lifetime (default 15 minutes) unless explicitly requested for archival. Rotation cadence can be set in the playlist (we set 90d default but can be changed).

2) Operator telemetry & minimization: the PDF lists the minimum telemetry retained for on-prem support (ops logs, scheduler traces, and failure dumps). We can gate full trace access behind a signed attestation + time-limited SSH/Bastion session that is captured in our audit logs. For compliance evidence, we can provide a redacted sample (anonymized) and a summary report for your audit team.

A couple of asks for NovaMed to speed review:
- Which CMK hosting option do you prefer (Cloud CMK vs HSM gateway)? If you lean HSM, please indicate preferred vendor/model so we can validate compatibility with our gateway.
- Do you need subprocessor names included directly in the DPA, or is a rolling notice + addendum acceptable? Some procurement teams prefer explicit lists; others accept the rolling notice model.

Irene Choi
Sr. Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

> - Notification model: explicit subproc list in DPA or rolling notice + 60/90-day windows.

3) I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call with NovaMed tomorrow morning PST; Irene will join for the technical review.
